[0] Apple is expected to announce the iPhone 18 series this fall as usual in September, but this year's rollout will echo the unusual circumstances of the 2020 COVID-era iPhone launch in several ways.

[1] How this fall's iPhone launch differs from Apple's usual pattern

[2] Apple has many hugely successful products, but the iPhone has always been its crown jewel, accounting for a huge share of the company's overall revenue.

[3] So it makes sense that Apple tries to keep iPhone launches consistent. By maintaining a predictable new iPhone release schedule, it keeps Wall Street and consumers happy.

[4] Typically, Apple unveils new iPhones in early September — usually four new models — and ships them all later that same month.

[5] However, 2020 was an exception due to COVID-related reasons.

[6] The 2020 fall iPhone lineup wasn't announced until October, and initially only two of the new models went on sale, with the other two delayed until November.

[7] This year, rumors suggest Apple will see some similar unusual aspects to its launch plan.

[8] Although the September announcement is still expected, Apple may not release all new iPhone models at the same time.

[9] Like in 2020, only two models may be available initially: the iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone 18 Pro Max.

[10] The highly anticipated foldable iPhone Ultra is expected to be unveiled in September, but rumors suggest its launch date may be slightly delayed, possibly arriving weeks after the Pro models.

[11] Apple may also deviate from its usual approach when it comes to the total number of iPhone models.

[12] If rumors of the iPhone 18 and iPhone Air 2 being delayed until spring 2027 are accurate, only three new models would debut this fall — making it the smallest fall iPhone lineup since 2019.

[13] Whether for strategic reasons, or due to a global memory chip shortage and the challenges of mass-producing an entirely new foldable device, Apple's fall 2026 launch could echo several aspects of 2020.

[14] What features are you hoping Apple brings to this fall's iPhone launch? Let us know in the comments.
